trap-superlative.evidence: "Every particle interaction corresponds to a transfer matrix" and the catalogue's physical assignments are asserted rather than derived, and three checkable claims in the block do not hold up. (1) SELF-REFERENTIAL DEFINITION: M_i is defined as the product, "M_i = prod_j T_j(q)", and then the Groebner-Shirshov ideal is defined as I_i = ker(prod_j T_j(q) - M_i(q)) - the argument of ker is identically the zero matrix, so I_i is the whole space and the definition says nothing. (2) The eigenvalue expression is correct but unsimplified, and the simplification matters: T_{gamma e} = T_pp encodes sigma, whose characteristic polynomial lambda^2 - (q - q^-1)lambda - 1 factors as (lambda - q)(lambda + q^-1), so lambda_+ = q and lambda_- = -q^-1 EXACTLY - the eigenvalues AGENTS 7a names for sigma_i. I confirmed numerically at the proton pin: lambda_+ - q = -2e-31 at 30 dps. (3) Consequently E_n proportional to lambda_+^n = q^n GROWS geometrically in the shell index (1.110, 1.232, 1.368, 1.518, 1.685 for n = 1..5), and Delta E_{n->n+1} grows with it; the hydrogen shell energies it is offered as a model of converge instead. The block does not claim a numerical match, but "This gives the photon energy for shell transitions" is stated without that caveat. (4) The sequential-composition rule Delta_total = Delta_2 T_between Delta_1 + Delta_1 + Delta_2 does not follow from the stated definitions: substituting T_i -> T_i + Delta_i into a product gives Delta_2 T_b T_1 + T_2 T_b Delta_1 + Delta_2 T_b Delta_1, which is not the printed expression.
trap-superlative.notes: Reported, not edited (all mathematical). Routes: (1) define M_i as the reduced normal form and I_i as the kernel of the reduction map, or drop the ker formulation; (2) replace the radical with lambda_+ = q, lambda_- = -q^-1 and cite 7a; (3) state explicitly that E_n proportional to q^n is a growth law and is not offered as the Rydberg spectrum; (4) re-derive the sequential rule or mark it as a definition rather than a consequence. Verified separately and CORRECT: a' = ac(q-q^-1) + ad + bc and b' = ac + bd are exactly the coefficients of (c sigma + d)(a sigma + b) reduced by sigma^2 = (q-q^-1)sigma + 1, and the matrix form [a';b'] = T[a;b] reproduces them; trace and determinant claims elsewhere in the chain also hold.
